actual_checks: All exact prompt/report/source records read; no prior contributions listed. Complete singleton topological leaf-class scope is C2 foliations on closed connected orientable 3-manifolds. Coarse classification is not inferred from this topological theorem.

Q-linear independence of covector coordinates makes the integer deck stabilizer of each affine plane zero. Thus leaves have intrinsic topology R2, even though their images may be dense. A primitive v with a.v nonzero gives one embedded closed transversal, and t=(a.x)/(a.v) shows it meets every leaf.

Any lifted periodic smooth ambient metric admits uniform positive Euclidean quadratic-form bounds by compactness. Restricting to each affine plane and comparing all path lengths, with straight segments for the upper bound, gives uniform bilipschitz constants sqrt(m),sqrt(M). This uses the intrinsic leaf metric and does not confuse ambient/subspace distances or infer metric control from a foliation homeomorphism.
